messages.subject: Registering SWC morphologies for cluster analysis
messages.subject_clean: Registering SWC morphologies for cluster analysis
messages.body_plain:
Firstly I want to thank Greg for his previous response in "Re: NBLAST with SWC file format". I was able to easily apply clustering to the SWC files from the tutorial provided!
I have, however, encountered a problem with the results. It seems that the clustering is more impacted by the global position of the cells than their branching morphology as shown in the attached screenshot. Since the global position of the SWC files are not meaningful here I was hoping to transform the morphologies so they are positioned together. I believe I need to perform some type of registration/transformation on the SWC files (or neuronlist) so that they have the same global position and orientation. This way the clustering will focus more on the specific branching structures of the cells. If you have any documentation on this it would be greatly appreciated.

Best regards,
Evan

messages.body_plain:
Just an update on this issue. I found some useful work on co-registration of SWC morphologies by maximizing volume overlap of the cell domain from the following work: https://bmcbioinformatics.biomedcentral.com/articles/10.1186/s12859-018-2136-z (the code repo: https://github.com/wachtlerlab/Reg-MaxS.git). I Plotted the results of the registration. This allowed NBLAST to differentiate more on single-cell morphology and less on the global position.

messages.body_plain:
(Sorry delayed message)

Dear Evan,

I am glad that you were able to make some first steps using the tutorials.

I am not sure of the source of your neurons but as discussed in Costa et al 2016 [1], NBLAST is specifically designed for neurons that are characterised by their position within a registered brain space and the branching morphology within that. The registration strategy that you might use will depend on the details of your source data. The same paper details our procedure for registering neurons in fly brains and you can find out more about the CMTK toolkit that we've used e.g.

All the best,

Greg.

[1] https://doi.org/10.1016/j.neuron.2016.06.012

messages.subject: creating neuronlists from nblast clusters
messages.body_plain:
Hello nat-user,

I have a question on how to work with the resulting nblast clusters. These seem simple but I'm new to R (and nat) so I'm not sure how to proceed.

First here is how I got my clusters:

nl <- read.neurons("/path/to/swc") # load cells as neuronlist
nld <- dotprops(nl) # convert neuronlist to vector cloud
scores <- nblast_allbyall(nld) # get nblast scores
hcnl <- nhclust(scoremat=scores) # cluster with nblast scores
library(dendroextras)
dnl <- colour_clusters(hcnl, k=3, groupLabels=TRUE)

So given the cluster objects hcnl and dnl how can I segment the three clusters into 3 neuronlists?

I need the lists because I want to save the individual clusters for external use (ie csv of names of cells in cluster 1 as cluster1.csv) and the more general plotting routines in nat for neuronlists.

Thanks for your time and the software!

Best wishes,
Evan

messages.body_plain:
Dear Evan,

Take a look at

subset(hcnl, k=3)
cutree(hcnl, k=3)
dendroextras::slice(hcnl, k=3)

There are differences in the cluster numbers (whether they are as plotted or in the order of occurrence of the input data items)

Best,

Greg.
